decisions.reason: As a core resin-injection unit aligned with the firm's announced technology path, several years of market presence and prior visible investment make management more inclined to continue supporting it than to admit failure now.

This product also sits in the firm's central application-equipment business, and a medium-sized German machinery maker would typically give such an invested, technically relevant platform a long commercial run rather than withdraw it quickly.

The automatic airless spray gun is close to the company's established spray portfolio, so accumulated development, documentation and channel support favor retention unless there is unmistakable evidence of persistent underperformance.

Because the manual airless spray gun fits the traditional offering and can still be justified as part of a complete customer solution set, management is likely to keep it on the market and attribute any weaker results to normal market variation.

As a multi-model product line in a core spray segment, it reflects the strongest public and commercial commitment, which under escalation of commitment makes withdrawal within a year especially unlikely.
